subject: Interregion billing & credit structure — draft terms and follow-ups
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@stellardata.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pricing ask: multi-region commit and blended rate?

Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're evaluating Redwood for production inference across our US and EU workloads, with a smaller APAC footprint. Before we loop procurement, can you confirm how you handle:

- Committed usage that spans regions (do you do blended per-token rates or separate regional commits?)
- How overage is billed if usage pads shift between regions month-to-month
- Any currency / VAT handling if we seat billing in EUR for our EU entity

I can send a CSV of last 3 months by region if that helps. High level: we expect ~700M tokens/month steady-state split ~60% US, 35% EU, 5% APAC, with occasional 2x spikes in EU around product launches.

Would like a back-of-envelope pricing for a 12-month commit and also an example contract flow.

—Liam
Stellar Data Labs
liam.oconnor@stellardata.com
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@stellardata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing ask: multi-region commit and blended rate?

Hi Liam —

Appreciate the detail — yes, a CSV would help. I attached a small template you can drop the numbers into (region-usage-breakdown.csv) — if you prefer, Marissa on my team can pull this together with you in a short call.

Quick answers:
- We offer both per-region commit pricing and a blended "global commit" option for customers who want a single invoice and simpler unit economics.
- Blended commits are priced by calculating a usage-weighted blended per-token rate at contract signing; month-to-month the system applies the blended rate across regions. For large sustained shifts we can recalc at quarter boundaries.
- Overage can be billed at the on-demand regional rate, or applied against pre-purchased token credits (your choice in the MPA). We commonly include a 10% buffer credit so normal variability doesn't trigger overage.
- Currency and VAT: we can invoice USD or EUR. VAT handling follows local regs; if you need a EUR invoice from your EU entity we can support that.

Next steps: if you send the CSV I’ll run a quick blended estimate and loop Ben for a pricing matrix and Karhtik for cross-region routing notes (to ensure latency/cost tradeoffs are clear). If procurement is ready, we can attach a draft MPA for legal review.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt

Subject: RE: Pricing ask: multi-region commit and blended rate? — draft matrix

Hi Liam / team —

Thanks for the usage outline. I put together a quick draft pricing matrix (attached: draft-pricing-matrix.xlsx) showing two approaches:

Option A — Regional commits (separate commitments per region):
- US committed tier 600M tokens/mo => $0.0018/token
- EU committed tier 400M tokens/mo => $0.0020/token
- APAC committed tier 50M tokens/mo => $0.0022/token
- Benefits: per-region SLOs, simpler capacity guarantees in Dedicated mode

Option B — Global blended 12-month commit (single invoice):
- Example blended calc (based on your 60/35/5 split at 700M tokens): weighted avg => $0.00188/token
- 12-month commit discount ladder: 10% at >5M tokens/mo baseline, 18% at >20M tokens/mo baseline (example tiers)
- Includes 10% usage buffer applied monthly before overage billing

Other commercial notes:
- Overage: charged at on-demand regional rate or deducted from purchased token credits; we can cap monthly overage at 20% for enterprise customers with a penalty discount schedule.
- Rollover: unused committed tokens can optionally roll quarterly (not monthly) — can be enabled for an additional 0.5% contract uplift.
- Currency: we can invoice in EUR; net-of-VAT or VAT-inclusive is selectable on the invoice; taxes passed through.
- Audit & compliance: SOC 2 Type II and data residency options available; we’ll include the SOC letter and evidence in the MPA appendix.

If you like Option B we’ll run a precise blended calc once we have the CSV. We can also draft a DocuSign-ready MPA with the billing and routing appendices.

—Ben

Subject: Re: Pricing ask: multi-region commit and blended rate? — procurement questions

Team —

Thanks for the early matrix. A few procurement/legal clarifications before we proceed:

1) Rollover / credits: can you confirm the mechanics (quarterly rollover vs monthly) and whether we can get a 12-month lookback true-up vs. forward-only credit?
2) Currency & invoicing: we prefer EUR invoices for EU spend. Will Redwood provide EUR invoices from an EU subsidiary or do we handle FX on our side?
3) Taxes: are VAT amounts shown on the invoice or billed separately?
4) Data residency and routing: we need assurance that EU tokens originating from EU customers will not be egressed to US-only hosts for inference. If routing to US happens, what controls/notifications are offered?
5) SOC 2 & logs: please attach SOC 2 letter and confirm retention window for audit logs (we need >= 12 months).

I’ve attached our standard PO template for your procurement team to review (PO-template.pdf). Please call out any non-standard commercial terms — specifically we have an internal policy limiting prepayment exposure and prefer monthly invoicing against committed credits.

Procurement
Stellar Data Labs
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Procurement <procurement@stellardata.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@stellardata.com>

Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2026 15:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing ask: multi-region commit and blended rate? — procurement questions

Hi —

Thanks — good questions. Quick replies inline and next steps below. Full answers / legal language will be reflected in the MPA we’ll circulate. I attached a draft MPA for review (redwood-draft-mpa.pdf).

1) Rollover / credits: we can enable quarterly rollover for committed tokens. We do not generally do historical lookbacks for credits by default, but we can negotiate a 12-month true-up for enterprise customers as a contract clause.
2) EUR invoices: we can issue EUR invoices via our EMEA billing entity; I’ve cc'd Karthik (EMEA finance) to confirm the legal entity details and tax handling.
3) Taxes & VAT: VAT will be shown on the invoice where applicable; if you need net-of-VAT pricing we can provide that line item.
4) Data residency / routing: Redwood Private is the recommended approach for strict EU-only inference. For Hosted API blended commits, we can lock routing policies so EU-originated requests are routed to EU-backed capacity; we’ll document the routing policy in Appendix A and add a clause for notification if cross-region routing is required for capacity.
5) SOC 2 & logs: SOC 2 Type II report is attachable; standard audit log retention is 12 months and can be extended for a fee.

Next steps:
- Liam: please upload the CSV to the HubSpot deal (link below) or send to Marissa so we can finalize a blended calc.
- Ben / Legal: incorporate procurement asks into the MPA draft and highlight any non-standard uplift for quarterly rollover or extended retention.
- Procurement: once the MPA addresses the items above, we can move to commercial sign-off and a pilot commit (we recommend a 3–4 week pilot commit to validate traffic patterns).

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1187

Thanks everyone — I’ll set a 30-minute sync for Friday to run the blended numbers live unless you prefer asynchronous.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
